gaps.lead: He jogged every morning when he was younger.
gaps.sentence: He ___ every morning when he was younger.
gaps.explanation: 'Used to + infinitive' describes a past habit.

gaps.lead: It wasn't necessary for her to bring any food — there was plenty.
gaps.explanation: needn't have + participle = it wasn't necessary, but she did it.

gaps.lead: I'd love to be able to afford a bigger flat.
gaps.explanation: wish + subject + could expresses regret about ability or possibility.

gaps.lead: He didn't study, so he failed the exam.
gaps.sentence: If he had studied, he ___ the exam.
gaps.explanation: If + past perfect, would have + past participle.

gaps.lead: No changes will be made to this project.
gaps.hint: go ahead = proceed; according to plan
gaps.explanation: 'No changes' means the project 'will go ahead according to plan'.

gaps.lead: The company is unable to guarantee an allocated car-parking space to all employees.
gaps.sentence: The company's employees shouldn't ___ allocated a car-parking space.
gaps.explanation: 'Count on being allocated' means rely on receiving.
